scope: SQLite transactions and atomic invariants, error rollback, concurrent control mutations; src/store.ts (reachability traced through src/coordinator.ts, src/security.ts, src/cli/overview.ts, src/runtime.ts, src/mcp.ts)

findings.title: Stale `error` survives finish()'s re-arm of a failed worker to `ready`
findings.evidence: finish() writes `error: result.summary` on the transition to the terminal result state (src/store.ts:294), then re-arms a worker that still has a queued dispatch with `this.transition(id, "ready", { completed_at: null })` (src/store.ts:296-297). transition() merges supplied fields over the stored worker (src/store.ts:146-152), so the failure summary persists. The sibling re-arm path in queueMessage explicitly passes `error: null` (src/coordinator.ts:239-243), so the two disagree.
findings.reproduction: Local fake provider/agent from tests/helpers (no cloud calls). Worker to running; coordinator.message(follow-up); agent.complete({status:'failed', summary:'lint gate failed'}); await coordinator.tick(). Result: state = "ready", error = "lint gate failed", completed_at = null. publicWorker() returns {state:'ready', error:'lint gate failed'}. See /tmp/rev11/probe/p8.ts and /tmp/rev11/probe/p12.ts (both exit 0).
findings.recommendation: Clear terminal-only fields on re-arm: `this.transition(id, "ready", { completed_at: null, error: null })`, or normalise error/deadline_at inside transition() whenever the target state is non-terminal.
findings.confidence: high - reproduced end-to-end; consumers are display-only (src/security.ts:146, src/cli/overview.ts:232, src/runtime.ts:94), so impact is observability rather than state-machine corruption

findings.title: cancelDispatches() is the only multi-row mutation in store.ts with no transaction, and is never paired atomically with the terminal transition
findings.evidence: cancelDispatches() (src/store.ts:246-250) loops dispatches calling saveDispatch(), each an independent implicit commit. Every other multi-statement invariant wraps this.db.transaction(...): create (:71), transition (:158), claimDispatch (:252), finish (:278). Coordinator always calls cancelDispatches() then a separate transition() (src/coordinator.ts:411-418, :489-495, :775-783, :799-804, :894-905, :935-958, :968-975), so 'all dispatches cancelled AND worker terminal' is never a single commit. The two statements are synchronous with no await between them, so there is no JS interleaving window; a crash window requires killing the process mid-window.
findings.reproduction: Injected a throw on the 2nd saveDispatch inside cancelDispatches: resulting dispatch states were ["cancelled", "pending", "pending"] (partial cancellation). See /tmp/rev11/probe/p7.ts (exit 0). Crash-window impact traced by code: a worker left in running/waiting with all dispatches cancelled falls through monitor() to transition 'waiting' (src/coordinator.ts:536-539) until deadline_at (set at src/store.ts:256) trips the timeout check at src/coordinator.ts:452-455.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the loop in this.db.transaction(...)(). Stronger: add one store method that cancels dispatches and applies the terminal transition in a single transaction, and replace every cancelDispatches()+transition() pair in the coordinator with it.
findings.confidence: high for the atomicity gap (reproduced); medium for real-world impact, which is bounded by the single-writer process lock (src/runtime.ts:145) and busy_timeout=5000 (src/store.ts:22)

findings.title: request_id retry idempotency depends on the config-resolved SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
findings.evidence: create() fingerprints the resolved input: `createHash("sha256").update(JSON.stringify(input))` (src/store.ts:72-74). input is built by Coordinator.spawn, which fills timeout_seconds from config.SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS when the caller omits it (src/coordinator.ts:185-190). src/store.ts:81-82 then throws "request_id already used with different arguments" on mismatch, so an operator setting is baked into the idempotency key.
findings.reproduction: Two Coordinator instances over one Store differing only in SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (3600 -> 1800), same request_id and identical body: retry rejected with 'request_id already used with different arguments'. See /tmp/rev11/probe/p11.ts (exit 0).
findings.recommendation: Fingerprint only caller-supplied arguments (hash the spawnSchema output before timeout_seconds is resolved) and treat the effective timeout as mutable metadata, or compare a canonicalised subset (team/task/role/prompt) and log rather than reject a timeout-only difference.
findings.confidence: high - reproduced; not covered by tests/lifecycle.test.ts:13-17 or tests/core.test.ts:88-120, which retry under unchanged config with an explicit timeout_seconds. Breaks the documented 'use request_id for safe retries' contract (src/mcp.ts:73, ARCHITECTURE.md)

limitations: store.ts is unchanged between baseline 5672ead and target d428e0f, so this assesses pre-existing code rather than the branch delta.
Full test suite intentionally not run (reserved for the whole-suite reviewer); only the store/targeted suites above.
Multi-process concurrent writers not exercised beyond a two-connection probe; the flock plus documented single-owner deployment makes that path unreachable.
Filesystem-permission and redaction surfaces only spot-checked (WAL/SHM inherit 0600) and belong to other reviewers' scopes.
No real cloud, model or infrastructure calls: all providers and the coding agent were local fakes.
